editorial:
Imagine being a smart, driven student with your whole life planned out, only to have one short romance flip your world upside down. You will meet Rosamund, a doctoral student working at the British Museum who finds herself pregnant by a newsreader. While her best friend tells her to reconsider, Rosamund is determined to do it all on her own. She wants to finish her degree and raise her child without depending on anyone. It is a quiet, grounded story that feels very real, focusing on the stress and hope of a woman trying to break the mold of what society expected from mothers back in the sixties.

What really makes this work is how the movie handles the sudden shift in tone when the baby actually arrives. The acting is understated and natural, making you feel every bit of Rosamund's anxiety. While the pace is slow, it builds a lot of tension regarding her independence. If you enjoy character studies about strong women, you should definitely check this out. You can find it by renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection if you want the best picture quality for your home theater.
endingExplained: After the baby is born, you see that Rosamund faces a huge challenge when the child has health issues. Her plan to be a perfectly self-sufficient mother falls apart as she realizes she cannot do everything alone. In the final scenes, she has to let go of her pride and accept help from others. The movie ends with her finding a new balance between her intellectual goals and the messy reality of motherhood.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves realistic stories about personal growth and motherhood.
